terms.comment: A day kept for the gods, as against a working day, diēs profēstus (Plaut. Aul. 380–381); a festival of several days is diēs fēstī or fēriae. Most Roman festivals are neuter plurals: Sāturnālia, Parīlia.
Days of rest kept for a festival; also the holidays (see holidays).
Poetic and late Latin for diēs fēstus (Lewis & Short); in Church Latin a feast of the Church (fēstum nātīvitātis Chrīstī, Traupman 291).

terms.gloss: a festive celebration; a crowded gathering
terms.comment: The keeping of a feast or games by many people together; first, any crowded gathering: quae domus? quae celebrātiō cottīdiāna? (Cic. Sull. 73).

phrases.latin: Kal., Īdibus, Nōnīs, fēstus diēs cum erit, corōnam in focum indat
phrases.english: on the Kalends, the Ides and the Nones, and whenever there is a feast day, she is to put a garland on the hearth
on the Saturnalia, the best of days!

festus.html: De Vaan 212, s.v. fēriae: fēriae and fēstus rest on *fēs-, “divine, holy”.
